newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales grow fastest in nine months - BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales grow fastest in nine months - BRC.

text.p: British retail sales grew by 5.2 percent in the year to July, the fastest growth rate in nine months, the British Retail Consortium said on Tuesday.
In June, sales rose 4.5 percent on a like-for-like basis in value terms. Sales growth averaged 4.8 percent over the last three months, indicating generally buoyant growth.

A flood of windfall payments from building societies converting into banks -- 35 billion pounds in free shares at the last count -- appear to have been spent on home improvements or one-off purchases such as dishwashers or computers, the BRC said.

"This month's rise in the rate of sales growth is not...surprising," said BRC director-general Ann Robinson. "The summer sales have provided extremely good value this year, and customers with windfall gains to spend have been able to take advantage."
But four quarter-point interest rate rises since May -- the last came just five days ago, taking base rates to seven percent -- will limit high street spending in future months, she said.

Andrew Sentance, chief economic advisor to the BRC, said July's sales figures did not fully reflect the impact of the slew of post-election rate rises, which are only starting to feed through to consumers.
"They will be reinforced by the impact of the strong pound which pushes down inflation directly and slows the economy through its effect on the manufacturing sector," he said.
The Bank of England may already have tightened monetary policy far enough to ensure slower growth and subdued inflation next year, he added.
The BRC said better weather in July boosted late purchases of sandals and summer fashions. Clothing sales as a whole were well up on June.
Sales of white goods, televisions, audio equipment and videos were strong, as were furniture and sales orders.
But London stores continue to suffer from low tourist spending, because of the overwhelming strength of the pound -- up more than 20 percent in a year, despite a sharp slide late last week.
